phases.label: Day 1: trabectedin

medicines.name: Dexamethasone
medicines.note: Required anti-sickness premedication that appears to help reduce liver toxicity. Do not add the generic 8 mg steroid reference on top; reconcile all support steroids.

medicines.name: Individual anti-sickness prescription
medicines.timing: The team specifies prevention, delayed-sickness and rescue timing
medicines.note: Reconcile interactions and the actual support prescription; this reference does not authorise self-treatment.

additional_support: Dexamethasone 20 mg intravenously 30 minutes before each infusion is required for anti-sickness treatment and appears to help reduce liver toxicity. This regimen has moderate nausea/vomiting risk; agree the complete prevention and rescue prescription without duplicate steroids. Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, a white-cell growth factor, may be used for low counts under local policy; it is not universally required.

Review all medicines and supplements, especially strong liver-enzyme inhibitors or inducers, statins and other liver-toxic medicines. Avoid alcohol. Confirm steroid premedication, blood tests, pump training, line care, disconnection and verified contact numbers.

The team chooses appropriate intravenous access and explains its care. Report pain, burning, redness or swelling during treatment immediately. If a port or peripherally inserted central catheter is used, confirm dressing, flushing, infection precautions and eventual removal arrangements. Confirm spill or leak instructions and who to call if the pump alarms, becomes disconnected or appears to finish early. Never change settings or disconnect it yourself.
An improved test result does not authorise restarting after a safety hold; confirm the new prescription.
Olanzapine may be added for breakthrough nausea/vomiting; cyclizine may be considered where the patient is not already receiving olanzapine.

Only optional additional antiemetic steroid may be adjusted after prescription reconciliation. Retain the required dexamethasone 20 mg intravenously 30 minutes before every trabectedin infusion; the generic omission advice does not apply to this required premedication.

Metoclopramide: adult maximum 10 mg up to three times daily (30 mg/day) and maximum treatment duration 5 days under current European Medicines Agency/Irish product information; avoid prolonged repeated use without review.

local_reference.label: CUH Department of Medical Oncology: Adjuvant medication prescription for chemotherapy Moderate Risk for nausea and vomiting, Version 2 (05/05/2021)
local_reference.note: The local CUH source is retained as a reference list, not as the national antiemetic standard. Nystatin/chlorhexidine are displayed as local mouth-care adjuncts, not universal antiemetic or mucositis prophylaxis. Verify current local oral-care policy. This historical local proforma needs current pharmacy confirmation. It is an alternative reference, not a second course to add automatically.

items.directions: Take once daily for two days starting the day after chemotherapy.
Take one capsule daily for three days starting on the day of chemotherapy.
Rinse 1 mL around the mouth four times daily after meals during the chemotherapy regimen.
Rinse 10 mL around the mouth for at least 1 minute four times daily; expel after rinsing.
Take one tablet three times daily as required.
Take one tablet three times daily as required.
Take 4 mg after the first episode of diarrhoea, then 2 mg after each further episode, to a maximum of 16 mg/day.

clinical_source_boundaries: Pretreatment gates include haemoglobin at least 9 g/dL, albumin at least 25 g/L, neutrophils at least 1.5 and platelets at least 100 ×10⁹/L, with source-specific liver and muscle-enzyme limits. Current results and previous-cycle toxicity are different inputs.
Creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min conflicts with the source organ table but fails its pretreatment gate and current product criteria; do not infer treatment clearance from a no-adjustment row.
Source cardiac delay/reduction and discontinuation wording needs clinical adjudication. Prior permanent-stop history remains relevant after numerical recovery.
The source dose ladder is 1.5 to 1.2 to 1 mg/m²; do not re-escalate after a toxicity reduction. This education is not a dose calculator.

phases.label: Day 1: vinblastine and methotrexate

medicines.name: Individual anti-sickness prescription
medicines.timing: The team specifies prevention, delayed-sickness and rescue timing
medicines.note: Reconcile interactions and the actual support prescription; this reference does not authorise self-treatment.

additional_support: Methotrexate has low and vinblastine minimal nausea/vomiting risk. National Cancer Control Programme lists no usual separate premedication or routine additional prophylaxis. Use individual anti-sickness, mouth and constipation support. The team prescribes any rescue medicines, extra hydration or white-cell growth-factor injections individually; the separate high-dose methotrexate support programme does not automatically apply.

Ask oncology/pharmacy before taking anti-inflammatory painkillers, trimethoprim or co-trimoxazole, other antibiotics, proton-pump inhibitors, folate supplements or new medicines. Avoid alcohol. Tell anaesthesia staff about methotrexate before procedures, including possible nitrous oxide use. Do not self-stop essential medicines; have the complete list reconciled.

The team chooses appropriate intravenous access and explains its care. Report pain, burning, redness or swelling during treatment immediately. If a port or peripherally inserted central catheter is used, confirm dressing, flushing, infection precautions and eventual removal arrangements.
An improved test result does not authorise restarting after a safety hold; confirm the new prescription.

clinical_source_boundaries: Methotrexate kidney thresholds disagree: NCCP permits no adjustment at creatinine clearance at least 50 mL/min but also lists half dose at 20–50; the current referenced product uses above 60 full, 30–59 half and below 30 contraindicated. Exactly 50 and the 50–60 interval require reconciliation; severe impairment cannot bypass the regimen exclusion.

Methotrexate liver limits also differ narrowly: NCCP avoid above 86 micromol/L bilirubin versus current product contraindication above 85.5. Vinblastine product wording uses direct bilirubin, whereas the regimen table is less specific. Confirm the analyte and prescription.

Grade 1 mucositis calls for 50% methotrexate review; grade 2 requires a 100% reduction, meaning omit. No numeric restart formula is supplied; higher-grade disease and actual mouth/gut ulcers need separate review.
A delay of at least two weeks reduces baseline vinblastine by 25%, not methotrexate and not necessarily 25% of an already reduced dose.
Large third-space fluid collections are an exclusion because methotrexate can accumulate. Current symptoms and previous suspected drug-induced lung disease remain separate safety inputs.
